newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo to reduce Lonrho stake - sources.
newsitem.headline: Anglo to reduce Lonrho stake - sources.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd will settle its dispute with the European Commission over its 25.8 percent stake in Lonrho Plc, sources close to Anglo told Reuters on Friday.
The sources also said that Anglo would reduce its Lonrho stake to less than 10 percent over a period of two years.

"After much deliberation, Anglo American Corporation tipped the view that a settlement of this nature was better than the uncertainty of a battle in court and agreed with great reluctance to accept the Commission's proposal," a source close to Anglo said.

The sources said that the European Commission (EC) said that the Anglo stake and shares held by Southern Life (1.6 percent of Lonrho) would have given it a majority of the vote cast at any shareholders' meeting.

They said formal announcements could be expected next week -- probably Wednesday -- after which a voting trust, in which the remainder of the shares would be held, will be set up within a couple of weeks.
"We assume there will be a formal announcement next week, probably Wednesday," one of the sources said.

Anglo initially proposed placing 5.84 percent of the Lonrho capital in a voting trust and the company would also have provided certain ring-fencing undertakings which would have isolated Anglo's influence on Lonrho's platinum interests.
Lonrho controls 73 percent of its platinum divisions in South Africa.
Anglo's platinum group Anglo American Platinum Corp produces around 38 percent of the world's newly-mined platinum.
The EU said that Anglo's stake in Lonrho, coupled with its extensive platinum interests in South Africa was incompatible with the bloc's competition rules.
Anglo could still decide to whom its Lonrho shares should be sold, but this would have to be approved by the EC.
"It's up to the Commission to decide who the list of disqualified buyers are," one source said.
